mainTopic: The end of the רחב story, offerings brought by גוים outside the מקדש, דוד's purchase of the altar site, and the camps of the wilderness, ירושלים and שילה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the אגדה about רחב הזונה: how she knew the fear of the Canaanite leaders, her age, and her conversion at fifty. The גמרא then learns from 'דבר אל בני ישראל' that the ban on שחוטי חוץ applies only to Jews, so a גוי may offer on his own במה even today. רב אסי says a Jew may not help or act as the גוי's messenger, and רבה says a Jew may still teach him how. The story of רבא and the offering of איפרא הורמיז shows this in practice. אביי asks why רבא required new wood. That question leads to the ברייתא about the 50 and 600 shekels דוד paid ארונה, and to the meaning of the word מוריגים. Next the גמרא explains the משנה that קדשים קלים were eaten throughout the מחנה ישראל in the wilderness: the camp kept its status even while traveling. Finally, רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that שילה had only two camps, and רבה begins proving which camp was missing. That proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רחב's words mean the men lost all strength
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רחב's words 'no spirit rose in any man' are a polite way of saying the men had lost all physical strength from fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: רחב meant that the men were so afraid that they could not even become physically aroused.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this section about רחב's words to the spies. It says her phrase 'ולא קמה עוד רוח' describes how terrified the men of יריחו were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קמה, 'rose', is read in a physical sense, not only as 'courage'. So רחב was saying the fear was so deep that the men's bodies were affected. This sets up the next question: how could she know such a thing?

phrases.english: That they could not even become erect.
phrases.notes: This is about רחב's words in יהושע 2:11, 'no spirit rose any more in any man.' Here 'rose' is read in a physical sense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised just before this section about the extra phrase in רחב's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase seemed to repeat the idea that their hearts melted, or to speak only of courage.
steps.terutzMaskana: It describes physical weakness caused by fear, which is a new point.

steps.title: How did רחב know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רחב could know such a private detail about the men.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how did she know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רחב could know about the men's physical state. This question sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רחב's words mean what step 1 said, she is claiming firsthand knowledge. The גמרא wants to know where that knowledge came from.

phrases.english: And how did she know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of the explanation given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רחב's knowledge about the men's physical state.

steps.title: Every ruler had been with רחב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that every prince and ruler of that time had been with רחב, so she knew them personally.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: there was no prince or ruler who did not go to רחב the prostitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a teaching: all the leaders of that time had visited רחב. So she knew from experience what state they were in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why her report to the spies could be trusted. She was not guessing about the fear in כנען. She knew the most important men personally.

keyTerms.meaning: רחב the prostitute (or innkeeper), from ספר יהושע chapter 2

phrases.english: As the Master said:
You do not have any prince or ruler
who did not have relations with Rahab the prostitute.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: אֵין לָךְ כׇּל שַׂר וְנָגִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She knew the leaders personally, so she knew how afraid they were.

steps.title: רחב's age and her תשובה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים give רחב's timeline. She was ten at יציאת מצרים and lived as a prostitute for forty years. She converted at fifty and asked to be forgiven in the merit of saving the spies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: she was ten years old when Israel left מצרים. She was a prostitute all forty years Israel was in the מדבר. At fifty she converted and said: 'May I be forgiven in the merit of the rope, the window and the flax.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching about רחב. It gives her age and tells how she did תשובה and converted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten plus forty years in the מדבר makes her fifty when the spies came. She pointed to three things she used to save the spies, the rope, the window and the flax, as the merit for her forgiveness. This finishes the רחב story before the גמרא moves to a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: in the merit of, as a reward for

steps.whatToRemember: רחב converted at age fifty. She asked to be forgiven in the merit of risking her life to save the spies with the rope, the window and the flax.

phrases.english: They said: She was ten years old
when Israel left Egypt,
and she was a prostitute [all] forty years
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: that Israel was in the wilderness.
After fifty years, she converted,
she said: 'May I be forgiven'
'in the merit of the rope, window, and flax.'
phrases.notes: See יהושע 2:6 and 2:15. She hid the spies under flax, then let them down from her window by a rope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further teaching about רחב after the question and answer about her knowledge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רחב was a prostitute from age ten to fifty, then converted and asked forgiveness in the merit of saving the spies.

steps.title: Quoting the rule that gentiles may sacrifice outside today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to a line from an earlier ברייתא: today גוים are allowed to bring offerings outside the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: and גוים today are permitted to do so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from a ברייתא learned earlier. This is a setup line: the next step will ask for its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא discussed offerings brought before the משכן was built, when private altars were allowed. It added that גוים may still do this today, even though Jews may not. The גמרא now wants to examine that last line.

phrases.english: The Master said: And gentiles at this time
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא learned earlier about bringing offerings before the משכן was built.

phrases.english: are permitted to do so.
phrases.notes: 'Do so' means bring offerings outside the בית המקדש, on a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וְגוֹיִם בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רחב story and returns to an earlier ברייתא to examine one of its lines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גוים today may offer sacrifices outside the בית המקדש.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that גוים may bring offerings outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule quoted in step 5. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jews are forbidden to bring שחוטי חוץ, offerings slaughtered outside the בית המקדש. So the גמרא needs a source showing the ban does not apply to גוים.

keyTerms.meaning: from where are these things learned? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows גוים are not bound by the ban on שחוטי חוץ.

steps.title: The verse speaks only to Israel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'דבר אל בני ישראל' that only Jews are commanded about שחוטי חוץ. So every גוי may build his own במה and offer whatever he wants on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'Speak to the children of Israel'. The children of Israel are commanded about שחוטי חוץ, but גוים are not. Therefore each one may build himself a private altar and offer on it whatever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא points out that the פסוק forbidding שחוטי חוץ is addressed to בני ישראל only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 17:2 opens with 'speak to the children of Israel'. That limits the ban on offering outside to Jews. Since גוים were never given this command, each one may set up his own במה and offer any animal he chooses.

keyTerms.meaning: offerings slaughtered outside the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean offerings outside the בית המקדש are allowed in general. The ban on שחוטי חוץ fully applies to Jews. The ברייתא only says the command was never given to גוים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the rule that a גוי may build his own altar and bring offerings even today, when Jews may not.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'Speak to the children of Israel':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:2

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מְצוּוִין עַל שְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ,
phrases.english: the children of Israel are commanded about offerings slaughtered outside,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַגּוֹיִם מְצוּוִין עַל שְׁחוּטֵי חוּץ.
phrases.english: but gentiles are not commanded about offerings slaughtered outside.
Therefore each and every one
builds himself a private altar for himself,
and offers on it whatever he wishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: דַּבֵּר אֶל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק addresses only בני ישראל, so גוים are not bound by the ban on שחוטי חוץ.

steps.title: A Jew may not help gentiles sacrifice outside
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי rules that even though גוים may offer outside, a Jew may not help them or act as their messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רב אסי: it is forbidden to help them or to act as their agent.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a limit to the rule. The גוי may offer outside, but a Jew may not take part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission belongs only to the גוי. A Jew is still bound by the ban on offering outside, so he may not assist or carry out the offering on the גוי's behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: their agency, acting as their messenger

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Aḥa said that Rav Asi said:
It is forbidden to assist them and to act as their agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: אָסוּר לְסַיְּיעָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission of step 7: it applies to the גוי, not to a Jew who helps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may not help a גוי offer outside or act as his messenger to do so.

steps.title: But a Jew may teach them how
steps.stepSummary: רבה adds that a Jew may instruct גוים how to bring their offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: but to teach them is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds one more detail to רב אסי's rule. Helping with your hands is forbidden, but giving instruction is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Teaching is not taking part in the act itself. So it does not fall under the ban on helping or acting as an agent. The גוי does the offering himself.
steps.whatToRemember: גוים may offer on a private במה today. A Jew may not help them or be their messenger, but he may teach them how to do it.

phrases.english: Rabba said: But to instruct them is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב אסי's ban: instruction is not considered helping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew may instruct גוים how to offer sacrifices outside the בית המקדש.

steps.title: רבא arranges an offering for the Persian queen-mother
steps.stepSummary: An incident shows רבה's rule in action. רבא told his students how a גוי offering should be brought, without doing it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the time איפרא הורמיז, mother of King שבור, sent an offering to רבא with the message: 'Offer it for me for the sake of Heaven.' רבא told רב ספרא and רב אחא בר הונא: 'Go take two גוי youths who are alike. Find a spot of fresh silt brought up by the sea. Take new wood, make fire with a new fire-starter, and have them offer it for her for the sake of Heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רבה's rule from the last step. רבא only gave instructions, and the offering itself was done by גוים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because a Jew may not act as a גוי's messenger (step 8), רבא did not offer it himself. He only taught them how to do it. He also insisted on a fresh, unused place, new wood and new fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Silt or fresh land brought up by the sea

phrases.english: Like that incident where Ifra Hurmiz
the mother of King Shapur
sent an offering to Rava
she sent him a message
"Offer it up for me for the sake of Heaven"

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ לְרַב סָפְרָא וּלְרַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא
phrases.english: He said to Rav Safra and to Rav Acha bar Huna
Go and take two youths who are alike
phrases.notes: These youths are גוים. A Jew may not do the offering for them (step 8).

phrases.english: and see where the sea brings up fresh silt
phrases.notes: Fresh land from the sea has never been used by anyone.

phrases.english: and take new wood
and bring out fire from a new fire-starter
and offer it up for her for the sake of Heaven
phrases.notes: The word literally says 'for him,' but it means for the queen-mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבה's rule that a Jew may instruct גוים about their offerings.
steps.raayaObject: A Jew may instruct גוים how to offer, as long as he does not offer for them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of רבא and איפרא הורמיז

steps.title: אביי asks whose view requires new wood
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks which opinion רבא followed when he required new wood, and suggests רבי אלעזר בן שמוע.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Whose view is this? It is רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's. As a ברייתא teaches, רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says: just as the מזבח must be something an ordinary person never used, so too the wood must be wood an ordinary person never used.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks where רבא's demand for new wood comes from, and links it to רבי אלעזר בן שמוע. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע compares the wood to the מזבח. Neither may have been used for ordinary purposes before. That would explain why רבא wanted new wood.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion is this?
An ordinary person, for everyday use

phrases.english: Abaye said to him
Like whom? Like Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua says

phrases.aramaic: מָה מִזְבֵּחַ – שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בּוֹ הֶדְיוֹט
phrases.english: Just as the altar is something an ordinary person did not use

phrases.aramaic: אַף עֵצִים – שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן הֶדְיוֹט
phrases.english: so too the wood must be wood an ordinary person did not use

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source for one detail of רבא's instructions: the new wood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whose opinion requires new, unused wood for an offering?

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר בן שמוע agrees a במה is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the link: even רבי אלעזר בן שמוע admits that a private altar does not need new wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר בן שמוע agrees that for a במה it is not needed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on this suggestion. The offering of a גוי is on a במה, and for a במה even רבי אלעזר בן שמוע does not require new wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new-wood rule only applies to the מזבח of the מקדש. A גוי's private altar is a במה, so רבא's demand seems unnecessary by every opinion. The next step brings a ברייתא to prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar outside the מקדש

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ
phrases.english: But Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua agrees
regarding a private altar!
phrases.notes: He means that at a במה, new wood is not required.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ בְּבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source suggested in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's requirement of new wood for a גוי's offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע's rule does not apply to a במה, so it cannot be the source for requiring new wood at a גוי's private altar.

steps.title: Two פסוקים disagree about what דוד paid
steps.stepSummary: To support the challenge, a ברייתא points out that two פסוקים give different prices for דוד's purchase from ארונה: 600 gold shekels and 50 silver shekels.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: One פסוק says, 'דוד gave ארנן for the place six hundred gold shekels by weight.' Another says, 'דוד bought the threshing floor and the cattle for fifty silver shekels.' How do these fit together?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the claim in step 12. The ברייתא starts by pointing out a contradiction between two פסוקים, which it will resolve next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים describe the same purchase, but one says 600 and the other says 50. The answer in the next step will mention the wood, and the גמרא is building toward its point about wood at a במה.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse says (used to set up two verses that seem to clash)
How can this be? How do these fit together?

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא
One verse says
"And David gave to Ornan for the place

phrases.aramaic: שִׁקְלֵי זָהָב מִשְׁקָל שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְגוֹ׳״
phrases.english: gold shekels weighing six hundred, etc."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 21:25

phrases.english: And it is written
"And David bought the threshing floor and the cattle
for fifty shekels of silver"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 24:24

phrases.english: How can this be?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא that backs up the challenge in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע agrees that new wood is not needed at a במה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about דוד's purchase of the threshing floor from ארונה

steps.title: Two ways to fit the 50 and the 600 together
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives two answers. The first: דוד collected 50 from each tribe, which adds up to 600. The second, from רבי: 50 paid for the cattle, wood and altar spot, and 600 paid for the whole מקדש site.
steps.simpleTranslation: He collected fifty from each tribe, which comes to six hundred. רבי says in the name of אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי: the cattle, the wood and the altar spot cost fifty, and the whole area of the מקדש cost six hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question in two ways. The second answer mentions that wood was part of the 50-shekel purchase, which is the detail the גמרא needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first answer, both numbers describe one payment, counted in two ways. In רבי's answer they are two separate purchases, and the wood is part of the 50-shekel purchase. The actual support for the challenge in step 12 comes in the next step, when רבי אלעזר בן שמוע brings the פסוק showing what that wood was.

keyTerms.meaning: The entire area of the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate answers here. In the first, 50 and 600 are the same payment counted two ways. In רבי's answer, they are two different purchases.

phrases.english: He collected fifty from each and every tribe
which make six hundred

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי
phrases.english: Rebbi says in the name of Abba Yosei ben Dostai
the cattle, [and the wood,] and the place of the altar for fifty
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets ('and the wood') and some don't.

phrases.english: and the entire Temple site for six hundred

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'הא כיצד' question of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can 50 shekels and 600 shekels both describe דוד's purchase?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either 50 from each of the twelve tribes adds up to 600, or 50 paid for the cattle, wood and altar spot while 600 paid for the whole מקדש site.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע: farm tools were offered as wood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, who agrees with the split of 50 and 600. He brings a פסוק where ארונה offers his threshing tools to be used as altar wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן שמוע says: the cattle, wood and altar spot cost 50, and the whole Temple site cost 600. The proof is that ארונה told דוד: take the cattle for the עולה and the threshing boards and cattle equipment for wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it started in Step 13. This last opinion is the real support for the challenge in step 12 against רבא's demand for new wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ארונה's threshing tools were already used farm equipment, and they were offered as wood for דוד's altar. That altar counted as a private altar (במה). So this fits the claim in step 12 that even רבי אלעזר בן שמוע agrees a private altar does not need new wood.

keyTerms.meaning: the spot where the altar stands
the owner of the threshing floor that דוד bought

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Shammua says:
The cattle, the wood and the altar's spot for fifty,
and the whole Temple site for six hundred;
as it is written: "And Araunah said to David:
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 24:22

phrases.english: Let my lord the king take and offer [what is good in his eyes];
see, the cattle for the burnt offering,
and the threshing boards [and the cattle's equipment] for the wood."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא and gives the actual support for the challenge in step 12
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 12 that רבי אלעזר בן שמוע allows used wood on a private altar
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 24:22: ארונה offers his threshing tools as wood

steps.title: Defending רבא: the tools were new
steps.stepSummary: רבא can answer that ארונה's tools were also new, never used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would tell you: there too, it was talking about new tools.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא from the challenge in step 12 by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the tools were old and used. If they were new, the פסוק shows nothing about used wood. Then רבא can still hold like רבי אלעזר בן שמוע and require new wood.

keyTerms.meaning: and רבא would tell you (an answer given on his behalf)

phrases.english: And Rava would say to you:
There too, it was with new ones.
phrases.notes: "There" means ארונה's threshing tools in the פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the proof from Step 15 by saying the tools were new
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case in the proof (new tools, not used ones)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ארונה's tools were old, so used wood is fine on a private altar
steps.terutzMaskana: The tools may have been new, so רבא can still follow רבי אלעזר בן שמוע
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from step 12 does not stand. רבא's demand for new wood can still follow רבי אלעזר בן שמוע, because ארונה's tools may have been new.

steps.title: What are מוריגים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word מוריגים in the פסוק means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are מוריגים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain a hard word from the פסוק it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side question about a word. It does not change the halacha being discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: a word from the פסוק, explained in the next steps

phrases.english: What are morigim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק quoted in Step 15

steps.title: עולא: a טורבל bed
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that מוריגים is a 'מטה של טורבל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: it is a מטה של טורבל.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question, but uses a term that itself needs explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares the tool to a flat board shaped like a bed. The next step asks what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'turbal bed', a kind of flat board

phrases.english: Ulla said: a turbal bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17

steps.title: What is a טורבל bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what עולא's term means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a מטה של טורבל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of עולא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא's term was not clear enough, so the גמרא asks again.

phrases.english: What is a turbal bed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about עולא's term

steps.title: אביי: a toothed threshing board
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that it is a heavy board with teeth, used to thresh grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a heavy, toothed board that threshers thresh with.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a clear picture of the tool: a threshing board.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know that מוריגים were wooden threshing boards. That explains why ארונה could offer them as firewood.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A heavy toothed board that the threshers thresh with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a heavy toothed threshing board

steps.title: אביי's פסוק: a מורג with teeth
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a פסוק showing that a מורג is a threshing tool with sharp teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: what is the source? 'Behold, I have made you a new sharp threshing board with teeth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי supports his explanation with a פסוק that uses the same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls a מורג 'sharp' and 'with teeth', and uses it for threshing. That matches אביי's description exactly.

phrases.english: Abaye said: What is the verse?
"Behold, I have made you a new, sharp threshing board,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:15

phrases.english: having teeth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for Step 20
steps.raayaObject: אביי's explanation that מוריגים are toothed threshing boards

steps.title: רבא shows his son two פסוקים that clash
steps.stepSummary: While teaching his son, רבא points out that one פסוק says דוד paid 600 and another says 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא was teaching his son and set the פסוקים against each other: one says 'דוד gave ארנן...' (600 gold shekels), and one says 'דוד bought...' (50 silver shekels). How can both be true?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story of רבא raising the contradiction about דוד's payment with his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same contradiction the ברייתא raised in Step 13, now in a teaching scene. It sets up רבא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: set פסוקים against each other (pointed out a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the ברייתא repeating itself. It is a separate story about רבא teaching his son, and it will refine the answer from Step 14.

phrases.english: Rava was teaching verses to his son,
and he set the verses against each other for him:
It is written: "So David gave to Ornan..."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 21:25. That פסוק goes on to say six hundred shekels of gold.

phrases.english: and it is written: "So David bought..."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 24:24. That פסוק goes on to say fifty shekels of silver.

phrases.english: How can this be?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַקְרֵי לֵיהּ רָבָא לִבְרֵיהּ, וְרָמֵי לֵיהּ קְרָאֵי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the contradiction about the price from Step 13, through a story about רבא
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about דוד's payment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says 600 shekels and the other says 50, so they seem to contradict each other

steps.title: Fifty from each tribe makes 600
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that דוד collected 50 from each of the 12 tribes, and together that is 600.
steps.simpleTranslation: He collected 50 from each tribe, which adds up to 600.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction by saying both numbers are true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 50 is what each tribe gave, and 600 is the total from all 12 tribes. So the two פסוקים describe the same payment from two angles.

phrases.english: He collects fifty from each and every tribe,
which comes to six hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both numbers are correct: one is per tribe and one is the total
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two prices contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: 50 per tribe multiplied by 12 tribes equals 600

steps.title: But one says silver and one says gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוקים still clash, because one speaks of silver and the other of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they still contradict each other: there it says silver, and here it says gold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer of 50 times 12 fixed the numbers but not the metals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding up the tribes explains 50 versus 600. It does not explain why one פסוק says silver and the other says gold.

phrases.english: But they still contradict each other:
there it is silver, here it is gold!
phrases.notes: "There" is שמואל (silver), and "here" is דברי הימים (gold).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 23 as incomplete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The math works, but the metals are different, so the פסוקים still do not match

steps.title: Silver worth 600 gold shekels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא refines the answer: דוד collected silver whose total value equaled 600 gold shekels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what it means: he collected silver worth the weight of 600 gold shekels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the answer so that it works for both the numbers and the metals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The payment was made in silver, as שמואל says. Its total value was 600 shekels of gold, as דברי הימים says. So each פסוק describes a true side of the same payment.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, this is what it means

steps.whatToRemember: The two פסוקים describe one payment. It was made in silver, collected tribe by tribe, and its total was worth 600 gold shekels.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it means:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹבֶה כֶּסֶף בְּמִשְׁקַל שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת זָהָב.
phrases.english: He collects silver worth the weight of six hundred gold shekels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24 by refining the answer in Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refines the earlier answer: one פסוק names the metal paid, the other names its value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The silver and gold in the two פסוקים contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Silver was paid, and its total value equaled 600 gold shekels

steps.title: רב הונא explains 'throughout the camp of Israel'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that קדשים קלים were eaten throughout the מחנה ישראל. רב הונא explains this as anywhere Jews were, with no real camp boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says קדשים קלים are eaten throughout the camp of Israel. רב הונא says this means anywhere Jews were found, but there was no actual camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new line from the משנה about where קדשים קלים were eaten in the wilderness. רב הונא gives his explanation of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the words 'מחנה ישראל', which sound like a fixed area with borders. רב הונא reads them more loosely: the meat could be eaten wherever Jews were. He adds that there was no real 'camp' outside of which eating would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, such as שלמים, which may be eaten outside the courtyard
The camp of Israel, the outer area where the people lived

phrases.english: Offerings of lesser sanctity are eaten
[throughout the camp of Israel].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording; they finish the משנה's line, which isn't written out here.

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
In any of the places of Israel,
but there was no camp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּכׇל מְקוֹמוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, separate from the story about דוד's purchase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים קלים in the wilderness could be eaten anywhere Jews were, and there was no fixed camp boundary.

steps.title: רב נחמן proves there were camps in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא with a ברייתא. It describes a camp structure in the wilderness that is matched by three areas in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: were there no camps in the wilderness? A ברייתא teaches that just as there was a camp in the wilderness, so there is one in ירושלים. From the city walls to the הר הבית is the מחנה ישראל. From the הר הבית to שער ניקנור is the מחנה לויה. From there inward is the מחנה שכינה, which matches the area inside the curtains in the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב הונא's claim that there was no camp. He quotes a ברייתא that clearly lists separate camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said 'there was no camp.' The ברייתא says the wilderness had a real camp system, and that ירושלים copied it with three zones. If the wilderness model had defined camps, רב הונא's statement seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The Levite camp, the middle zone
The camp of the Divine Presence, the innermost zone
Nicanor's Gate, the entrance to the Temple courtyard
The curtains around the courtyard of the משכן

steps.confusionAlert: Three zones are being matched here. The מחנה ישראל runs from the city to the הר הבית. The מחנה לויה is the הר הבית itself. The מחנה שכינה is the courtyard. קדשים קלים belong to the outermost zone, the מחנה ישראל.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman raised an objection to Rav Huna:
And were there no camps in the wilderness?!
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Just as there was a camp in the wilderness,
so too there is a camp in Jerusalem;
from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount is the Israelite camp,
phrases.notes: 'From Jerusalem' means from the walls of the city.

phrases.aramaic: מֵהַר הַבַּיִת לְשַׁעַר נִקָּנוֹר – מַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה,
phrases.english: from the Temple Mount to Nicanor's Gate is the Levite camp,
from here onward is the camp of the Divine Presence,
and that is the same as the curtains in the wilderness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא: וּמַחֲנוֹת בְּמִדְבָּר לָא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רב הונא's statement from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that 'there was no camp.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא describes a real camp system in the wilderness, copied in ירושלים. That contradicts the claim that no camp existed.

steps.title: Rereading רב הונא: wherever the camp of Israel is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב הונא's words. They may be eaten wherever the מחנה ישראל happens to be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: they may be eaten wherever the Israelite camp is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב נחמן by changing how we read רב הונא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא did not deny that a camp existed. He meant the eating area was not one fixed spot: wherever the מחנה ישראל was set up, that was the place to eat. This fits the ברייתא, which agrees that there were camps.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (the statement should be read differently)

phrases.english: Rather, say:
wherever the Israelite camp is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: בְּכׇל מְקוֹם מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the אמורא's statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא seemed to say there was no camp at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא means the meat may be eaten wherever the מחנה ישראל was located, so the camp did exist.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב הונא needed to say something so obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the new reading: why would רב הונא need to teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wherever the Jews camped was, by definition, the מחנה ישראל. So saying 'they may be eaten wherever the מחנה ישראל is' seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why teach it?

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רב הונא given in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reread statement of רב הונא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it only means the camp is wherever the Jews were, it teaches nothing new.

steps.title: The meat does not become פסול as יוצא when the camp moves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא teaches a real point. We might have thought the meat became פסול as יוצא, and he teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said they became disqualified as having gone out; he teaches us that they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's statement is not obvious, because it rules out a mistake we could have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the camp traveled, the meat was carried out of the place where the camp had stood. We might think that makes it פסול as יוצא, meat that left its allowed area. רב הונא teaches that the allowed area moves with the camp, so the meat stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say (you might have thought)
Offering meat that left its permitted area, which makes it פסול
He teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: For קדשים קלים in the wilderness, the מחנה ישראל was wherever the camp was. When the camp traveled, the meat did not become פסול as יוצא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in the wilderness, the borders of the holy areas moved with the camp, unlike the fixed borders in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
they became disqualified as having gone out;
phrases.notes: He means when the camp traveled and the meat was carried out of where the camp had been.

phrases.english: he teaches us that they did not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: אִיפְּסִלוּ בְּיוֹצֵא; קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows a mistaken assumption that the statement rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meat carried out when the camp traveled would become פסול as יוצא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permitted area moves with the camp, so the meat is not פסול.

steps.title: Why not say the meat really becomes disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer and suggests the meat really does become פסול when the camp moves.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is true that the meat becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on what it just said. Maybe the meat really should become פסול as יוצא when the camp packs up and travels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30 the גמרא said רב הונא teaches that the meat does not become יוצא when the camp moves. Now it asks why we shouldn't accept that first idea. Once the camp is taken apart, there seems to be no camp left, so the meat looks like it is outside its proper place.

keyTerms.meaning: But say it is indeed so
Disqualified, not fit to eat as קדשים

phrases.english: But say it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe the meat really does become פסול when the camp moves, just as we first thought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 30 that the meat is not פסול as יוצא when the camp travels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A camp that has been taken apart seems to have lost its status, so the meat should count as having left the camp.

steps.title: The אהל מועד stays holy even while traveling
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק shows that the אהל מועד keeps its status while traveling, so the camp does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Then the אהל מועד shall travel.' Even though it traveled, it is still the אהל מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק. The Torah still calls it the אהל מועד while it is on the move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וְנָסַע אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד' use the name אהל מועד during the journey itself. This shows that moving does not remove the holy status. In the same way, the מחנה ישראל stays a camp while traveling, so meat carried along is not יוצא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, the משכן

steps.whatToRemember: A camp does not lose its holy status while it travels. That is why קדשים קלים carried along with the traveling camp do not become פסול as יוצא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the explanation of רב הונא: the meat may be eaten wherever the מחנה ישראל happens to be, even during travel.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Then the Tent of Meeting shall travel"
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:17

phrases.english: even though it traveled,
it is still the Tent of Meeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A traveling camp has lost its status, so the meat becomes יוצא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The camp keeps its status while traveling, just like the אהל מועד, so the meat stays fit.

steps.title: An extra area in ירושלים, and only two camps in שילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי adds a fourth area in ירושלים, the חיל of the עזרת נשים, and says שילה had only two camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: There was one more area, the חיל of the עזרת נשים, but people were not punished for entering it. And in שילה there were only two camps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the three areas of ירושלים mentioned earlier in step 27. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי adds one more area and says that in שילה there were only two camps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the three areas matching the camps in the wilderness, there was a fourth zone, the חיל of the עזרת נשים. It was off-limits to some people, but entering it did not bring a punishment. He also teaches that in שילה there were only two camps instead of three, which raises the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A rampart, an area just around the inner courtyards
The women's courtyard in the בית המקדש
Where the משכן stood after the wilderness, before the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
There was yet another one,
phrases.notes: One more area beyond the three areas in ירושלים from the earlier ברייתא.

phrases.english: and it is the rampart of the women's courtyard,
and they would not punish for it.
And in Shiloh there were not
anything but two camps alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the camps in ירושלים and שילה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was a fourth area in ירושלים, the חיל of the עזרת נשים, with no punishment for entering it. In שילה there were only two camps.

steps.title: Which camp was missing in שילה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the three wilderness camps did not exist in שילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one of them was not there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question about the ברייתא. If שילה had only two camps, which of the three camps was missing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wilderness there were three camps: the מחנה שכינה, the מחנה לויה, and the מחנה ישראל. The ברייתא said שילה had only two, but did not say which one was missing. The גמרא wants to know.

keyTerms.meaning: A camp, a zone with its own level of holiness

phrases.english: Which of them was not there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the ברייתא in step 33
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three camps was missing in שילה

steps.title: רבה: the מחנה לויה was there
steps.stepSummary: רבה says it makes sense that the מחנה לויה existed in שילה, and he begins to prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It makes sense that the Levite camp was there. Because if you think that the Levite camp was not there...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the מחנה לויה was present in שילה, so the missing camp must be the מחנה ישראל. He starts a proof here, and the proof continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה uses reasoning, not a quote, to answer. He starts with 'if you think the opposite,' so he will show a problem that would come up if there were no מחנה לויה. That problem is spelled out in the next lines of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
The Levite camp, the middle zone around the משכן
For if it would enter your mind, introducing the opposite idea in order to reject it

steps.confusionAlert: רבה's sentence is not finished here. He has only stated the opposite idea, and the problem with it comes right after.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה הֲוַאי;
phrases.english: Rabba said: It stands to reason that the Levite camp was there;
for if it would enter your mind
that the Levite camp was not there –

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: מִסְתַּבְּרָא דְּמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34 and begins a proof
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחנה לויה existed in שילה, so the missing camp was the מחנה ישראל. The proof continues in the next lines.
